relations.note: Later standardized genealogy makes Pincoya the daughter of the sea king Millalobo.
relations.source: Quintana, Chiloé mitológico; Cárdenas, El libro de la mitología

relations.note: Pincoya becomes a subordinate helper or princess within Millalobo’s marine kingdom.
Later genealogy identifies the human Huenchula as Pincoya’s mother.
Blume’s structural analysis classifies Pincoya as subordinate helper or servant to Huenchula.
The standardized later genealogy makes Pincoy and Pincoya siblings.
Later systematized tradition says Pincoya marries her brother Pincoy.
Pincoy accompanies or sings before Pincoya performs her shoreward or seaward dance.
relations.source: Plath, Geografía del mito y la leyenda chilenos

relations.note: Later standardized genealogy makes Pincoya and the Chilote Sirena sisters.

relations.myth: Complementary guardians of shore and sea
relations.note: Pincoya guards shellfish while Sirena guards fish, assigning them complementary maritime domains.
relations.source: Rosa Chiguay testimony, cited by Núñez

relations.note: Later retellings make Pincoya and Sirena jointly carry drowned sailors to the Caleuche.
Contested later retellings say Pincoya guides drowned sailors to the ghost ship Caleuche.
